Bug_Details:
computeIfAbsent passes the map key to the provided class's constructor With ambiguous constructor references used in java.util.Map#computeIfAbsent
function parameter, it becomes unclear what the code intends to do. map.computeIfAbsent(someLong, AtomicLong::new).incrementAndGet() map.computeIfAbsent(someLong, AtomicLong::new).incrementAndGet() Code of this form can seemingly look like it’s trying to make a counter,
creating the key if absent. Unfortunately the code is surprising, because it
will call the wrong AtomicLong constructor. Instead, it will create the
counter initialized with the key value, which is probably not desired.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is in the computeIfAbsent method where the key is passed to the AtomicLong constructor. Since AtomicLong has multiple constructors, it is unclear which one is being referred to, leading to unexpected behavior where the AtomicLong is not being initialized with the expected value but with the key itself.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case uses the value 10 as the key for the computeIfAbsent method. The method expects an AtomicLong constructor reference but instead it receives the key value itself. This leads to unexpected behavior where the AtomicLong is not being initialized with the expected value but with the key value itself.
